name: Phthalates
aliases: phthalates, ortho-phthalates, DEHP, DBP, BBP, DINP, DIDP, DCHP, DIOP, dicyclohexyl phthalate, diisooctyl phthalate, phthalic acid esters, plasticizers, ftalatos
what_is: Phthalates are chemicals used to make some plastics softer and more flexible. In food, exposure can come from packaging and other food-contact materials rather than from a deliberately added food ingredient.
why_botia: Studies have linked phthalate exposure with endometriosis and lower markers of ovarian reserve. Phthalates soften plastic and can migrate from food packaging into food — they are not listed as food ingredients, so BOTIA cannot detect them from the ingredient list. Women can show higher levels of some phthalates because cosmetics, perfume and other personal-care products are additional sources.
can_1: Explain why phthalates matter to the Woman layer and show the evidence linking exposure with endometriosis and lower markers of ovarian reserve.
can_2: Explain that food packaging is only one possible source and that cosmetics, perfume and other personal-care products can add to exposure.
cannot_1: Detect phthalates that migrate from packaging into food from an ordinary ingredient list.
cannot_2: Tell from a food label where a person's exposure came from or prove that phthalates caused endometriosis or reduced ovarian reserve.
